identity.name: Polysorbate 60
identity.chemical_class: Non-ionic emulsifier (polyoxyethylene sorbitan fatty acid ester)

function.mechanism: Amphiphilic polyoxyethylene-sorbitan fatty acid ester that lowers oil-water interfacial tension and stabilizes emulsions.

adi.basis: Group ADI for E432-E436 based on NOAEL 2500 mg/kg bw/day with UF 100 (EFSA re-evaluation).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation reported no safety concern at reported uses/levels, while noting scenario-dependent ADI exceedance in some younger groups in refined exposure scenarios.

adi.basis: ADI range 0-25 mg/kg bw; historical toxicological allocation (1973) with later specification-focused entry (2014).

concerns.summary: Older direct rat toxicology with polysorbate 60 reported increased lysosomal enzyme release and slightly increased intestinal permeability at experimental concentrations; modern class-wide emulsifier literature supports biological plausibility for gut barrier effects.
EFSA exposure scenarios indicated potential ADI exceedance in some younger subpopulations under refined/high-consumer scenarios, creating population-specific risk-management caveats.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA concluded no safety concern for reported uses and use levels within its re-evaluation framework.
Recent Korean dietary assessment found polysorbate 60 exposure well below ADI in assessed scenarios.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA refined scenario text indicates possible exceedance in younger groups; other population assessments report low average exposure.

risk_assessment.rationale: E435 remains approved with ADI-based controls, but EFSA scenario-dependent exceedance in younger populations and limited mechanistic GI concern signals argue against classifying it as risk_free/limited under all intake patterns.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI established at 25 mg/kg bw/day
Potential ADI exceedance in some younger/high-consumer scenarios
Recent intake studies often show exposure far below ADI
